title: Phishing & Social Engineering Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Protect yourself from phishing scams and social engineering attacks with this comprehensive privacy checklist. Learn to spot threats and stay secure.
intro: Phishing attacks and social engineering tactics are becoming increasingly sophisticated, with AI-generated content making scams harder to detect. This checklist provides actionable steps to protect yourself from fraudulent emails, fake websites, and manipulation attempts that target your personal information.

items.task: Enable two-factor authentication on all email accounts
items.why: Prevents attackers from accessing your email even if your password is compromised through phishing
items.howTo: Go to your email provider's security settings and enable 2FA using an authenticator app or SMS. Test the setup by logging out and back in.

items.task: Configure spam filters to maximum protection
items.why: Reduces the number of phishing emails that reach your inbox by automatically filtering suspicious content
items.howTo: In your email settings, set spam protection to 'High' or 'Aggressive'. Create custom filters to block emails with suspicious keywords or domains.

items.task: Disable automatic image loading in emails
items.why: Prevents tracking pixels from revealing when you open emails and stops malicious images from loading
items.howTo: In email settings, find 'Privacy' or 'Images' section and select 'Ask before loading external images' or disable automatic loading.

items.task: Set up email aliases for online shopping and signups
items.why: Limits exposure of your main email address and helps identify the source of phishing attempts
items.howTo: Create aliases through your email provider or use services like Apple Hide My Email. Use different aliases for shopping, newsletters, and accounts.

items.task: Enable email headers view for suspicious messages
items.why: Allows you to see technical details that can reveal fake sender addresses and routing information
items.howTo: Learn to access 'View Source' or 'Show Headers' in your email client. Look for mismatched sender domains and suspicious routing paths.

items.task: Install and configure Incognito Browser for secure browsing
items.why: Provides enhanced privacy protection and built-in security features to block malicious websites and trackers
items.howTo: Download Incognito Browser and enable features like anti-phishing protection, ad blocking, and privacy mode by default for all browsing sessions.

items.task: Enable browser phishing and malware protection
items.why: Warns you before visiting known malicious websites and blocks downloads of harmful files
items.howTo: In browser security settings, enable 'Safe Browsing' or equivalent. Ensure real-time protection and download scanning are active.

items.task: Install a reputable URL checker extension
items.why: Provides real-time analysis of links before you click them, identifying suspicious or malicious URLs
items.howTo: Install extensions like Web of Trust (WOT) or similar tools. Configure to show warnings for untrusted sites and scan all links automatically.

items.task: Disable password autofill for financial and sensitive sites
items.why: Prevents passwords from being automatically entered on fake websites that mimic legitimate services
items.howTo: In browser settings, go to password management and disable autofill for banking, email, and other sensitive accounts. Always type manually.

items.task: Bookmark legitimate websites for important services
items.why: Ensures you always visit the real website instead of clicking potentially malicious links in emails
items.howTo: Create bookmarks for your bank, email provider, shopping sites, and other frequently used services. Always use bookmarks instead of email links.

items.task: Configure browser to clear cookies and data regularly
items.why: Reduces tracking and prevents malicious websites from storing persistent data on your device
items.howTo: Set browser to clear cookies, cache, and browsing data on exit or weekly. Consider using private browsing mode for sensitive activities.

items.task: Create a personal verification process for unexpected contacts
items.why: Protects against impersonation attempts where attackers pretend to be colleagues, friends, or service providers
items.howTo: Establish a policy to verify unexpected requests through a different communication channel. Call back using known numbers, not provided ones.

items.task: Review and limit personal information on social media
items.why: Reduces the information available to attackers for creating personalized spear-phishing campaigns
items.howTo: Set profiles to private, remove personal details like birthday, phone, address. Limit posts about work, travel, and personal life.

items.task: Establish information sharing guidelines for family members
items.why: Prevents attackers from using family members as vectors to gather information or access accounts
items.howTo: Educate family about not sharing personal details over phone/email. Create code words for emergency situations and financial requests.

items.task: Set up fraud alerts with financial institutions
items.why: Provides early warning when someone attempts to access your accounts or open new ones in your name
items.howTo: Contact your bank and credit card companies to enable fraud monitoring. Set up account alerts for all transactions above a certain amount.

items.task: Practice the 'pause and verify' technique for urgent requests
items.why: Gives you time to think critically about requests that pressure you to act quickly, a common social engineering tactic
items.howTo: When receiving urgent requests for money, information, or access, take 24 hours to verify through independent channels before responding.

items.task: Document and report phishing attempts to authorities
items.why: Helps law enforcement track cybercriminals and prevents others from falling victim to the same scams
items.howTo: Forward phishing emails to the Anti-Phishing Working Group (reportphishing@apwg.org) and report to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

items.task: Create an incident response checklist for compromised accounts
items.why: Ensures you take quick, appropriate action if you fall victim to a phishing attack or account compromise
items.howTo: Write down steps: change passwords, enable 2FA, check account activity, contact institutions, monitor credit reports, document evidence.

items.task: Set up credit monitoring and identity theft protection
items.why: Provides early detection if your personal information is used to open accounts or make unauthorized transactions
items.howTo: Use free credit monitoring services or paid identity protection. Set up alerts for credit inquiries, new accounts, and address changes.

items.task: Maintain a secure backup of important documents and passwords
items.why: Ensures you can recover access to accounts and prove your identity if you become a victim of identity theft
items.howTo: Store encrypted copies of IDs, financial documents, and password manager backups in a secure location separate from your main devices.

items.task: Regularly test your phishing awareness with simulation tools
items.why: Helps you stay sharp at recognizing evolving phishing tactics and builds confidence in your detection abilities
items.howTo: Use free phishing simulation tools like those offered by security companies. Take online quizzes and review real-world examples regularly.

pro_tips: Trust your instincts - if something feels suspicious or too good to be true, it probably is. Take time to verify before taking action.
Legitimate companies will never ask for passwords or sensitive information via email. When in doubt, contact them directly using official channels.
Pay attention to urgency and emotional manipulation in messages. Scammers often create false deadlines to pressure quick decisions.
Keep your browser and security software updated. New phishing techniques emerge constantly, and updates include protection against them.
Consider using a dedicated email address for financial accounts that you never use for shopping, social media, or other online activities.
